svg.title: What are the critical points when assessing the respiratory rate of a 1-year-old? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: Least invasive first. Counting breaths needs nothing but your eyes, so it goes before the stethoscope, the cuff and the thermometer — every one of those means touching the child, and a crying toddler's respiratory rate is not his respiratory rate. For the same reason he stays in the parent's arms . A 1-year-old runs about 20 to 40 , averaging around 30 . Watch the abdomen, not the chest. Children under about 6 are diaphragmatic breathers — the belly is what moves, and counting chest rise loses breaths. And count a full minute, never 30 seconds doubled : infant and toddler breathing is normally irregular, so a half-minute count doubles the error along with the number. Undressing him fully is neither necessary nor kind in a cool room — and cold is its own problem.
